key_insight: Post-optimization corrections can improve ADAPT-VQE results without growing the ansatz, cutting both circuit depth and measurement cost.
engineering_relevance: These methods make quantum chemistry workflows more practical on near-term hardware by reducing adaptive-layer growth and lowering the experimental burden of Hamiltonian measurements.
method: Apply Hamiltonian-moment Krylov subspace diagonalization to an optimized ADAPT-VQE state.
Use identity-augmented q-sc-EOM to recover accuracy from truncated or sampled-ranked ansätze.
Avoid further nonlinear optimization or ansatz expansion after the initial ADAPT-VQE run.
evidence_signal: Across molecular systems up to 20 qubits, first-order Krylov correction reduced the iterations needed to reach the 1.6 mEh threshold by up to about 6×, with measurement-cost reductions up to about 40× under a resource-cost model.
watch_item: Benefits depend on a suitable resource-cost model and on the quality of the optimized/truncated starting state, so performance may vary for harder molecules or noisier hardware.
paper_title: Post-Optimization Subspace Corrections to Quantum Ansätze
